**Parity conditions for a number N with k digits:**
- **Product of digits is odd** ⟺ all digits are odd (any even digit makes the product even)
- **Sum of digits is odd** ⟺ the count of odd digits is odd. If all digits are odd, this means k must be odd

**No even-digit starting code works:** if N is even, its last digit is even, so P(N) is even — a generated value is even. ✗

**No even-length number works:** if k is even and all digits are odd, then S(N) = sum of k odd digits = even — a generated value is even. ✗

So candidates must have **all odd digits** and **odd length** k ∈ {1, 3, 5} (k=6 is even, excluded).

**Recursion terminates:** both operations strictly decrease multi-digit numbers, reaching single-digit fixed points. A single-digit d is "good" (all descendants odd) ⟺ d is odd, i.e., d ∈ {1,3,5,7,9}.

**No 2-digit or 4-digit number is ever good** (even length → sum is even), which constrains intermediate values.

## Defining "Good"

Good(N) ⟺ N is odd, Good(S(N)), and Good(P(N)).

Since 2-digit numbers are never good, any intermediate value that is 2-digit immediately fails.
